messages:
Maria: Evening all — taking primary for the 18:00-02:00 UTC window. Quick primer before I step into the bridge: small traffic burst expected from retail batch at 19:30 UTC, so pre-warm suggestions below.
Jake: noted — I'm secondary, reachable on pager and DM. I can jump if latency hits p99 for >5m.
Neha: thanks. two things: 1) confirm KV cache pre-warm in us-east-1, 2) reminders for fallback model order?
Maria: pre-warm plan: warm one replica in pool-A and one in pool-B with short synthetic prefixes. Command snippet:```bash
# pre-warm kv prefix for model small-llama
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/prewarm \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"small-llama","prefix":"/prewarm/retail-19:30"}'
```
Samir: also run a quick kv probe after prewarm:```bash
# kv probe
kubectl exec -it svc/kv-prober -- /bin/sh -c "python probe.py --model small-llama --seq 64"
```
Maria: fallback model chain we agreed in runbook: small-llama-q5 -> small-llama-8bit -> small-llama-4bit -> route to cached embeddings endpoint. If a pool shows sustained errors, auto-route to regional backup (eu-west-1).
Neha: adding runbook pointers: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference/prewarm-checks and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference/fallback-routing — keep these pinned during the window.
incidentbot: NOTE: Deploybot scheduled canary at 20:15 UTC for model-size-sweep. If canary starts failing, incident severity escalates to P1.
Jake: FYI — I'll hold deploy mitigation privileges. If canary fails, I'll flip canary -> hold and scale up dedicated pool:```bash
# immediately scale dedicated pool-A
inv scale pool-A --replicas 4 --priority reserved
```
Maria: coverage gaps: no one in APAC overnight, so if eu-west fails we might need to accept degraded throughput there. We'll enable soft-throttling to preserve control-plane stability:```json
{"throttle":{"route":"/v1/generate","limit_rps":40}}
```
Samir: quick triage checklist we use on pager: 1) check control plane errors (console -> tracing) 2) check GPU OOMs on nodes (kubectl describe pod) 3) verify kv hit-rate via metric: kv.cache.hit_ratio 4) if hit_ratio < 0.6, trigger prewarm and route to backup variant.
Neha: adding a one-liner to surface customer impact in the incident summary: "Users in region X may see increased latency or partial failures for generation endpoints; embeddings unaffected." Use this in incident title.
Maria: escalations: if >2 adjacent zones show errors or p99>3s for 10m, tag Sev2 and ping infra on-call (@Jake). If control-plane exceptions show new 5xx spike, open P1.
incidentbot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in us-east-1 (1.3s -> 3.6s) — auto-notify at 2m.
Jake: seeing the same in traces. Running prewarm now and bumping pool-A to 3 replicas.
Samir: I pushed a temporary route change to divert 20% of traffic to eu-west backup for retail-prefix:```bash
inv route set --route /v1/generate --weight eu-west-1=20
```
Neha: confirm kv probe after Samir's change?
Samir: probe shows kv.hit_ratio back to 0.72, latency improved to 1.5s.
Maria: sweet — keep an eye for 10m. If it stabilizes, we'll keep soft-throttle for 30m, then revert routing weights.
Jake: once stabilised, I'll cut a short post-incident note in #incidents with root-cause as 'cold kv cache + scheduled canary overlap'.
Neha: runbook shortcut list (pin these): - prewarm: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference/prewarm-checks - fallback: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference/fallback-routing - routing ops: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ops/route-change - kv probe tool: https://redwood.internal/tools/kv-prober
Maria: closing the handover note: primary till 02:00UTC, Jake secondary, Samir will monitor routing, Neha will own customer comms draft if we need to notify. Ping me if anything escalates. :thumbsup:
Jake: ack. I’ll stay on standby for 02:00UTC transition.
incidentbot: RESOLVED: latency trend back to baseline after prewarm and routing adjustment. Monitoring for 30m.
Maria: thanks team — logging actions and links in the rotation doc and will follow up in morning retro.
